blocks.text: It is our daily-life experience that an object projected upward comes back to the ground after rising to a certain height, because of the force of gravity acting downward. With increased initial velocity the object rises to a greater height before coming back. If we go on increasing the initial velocity, a stage comes when it will not return to the ground: it escapes from the influence of gravity.

blocks.title: Escape velocity
blocks.text: The initial velocity of an object with which it goes out of the Earth's gravitational field is known as the escape velocity.

The escape velocity corresponds to the initial kinetic energy gained by the body which carries it to an infinite distance from the surface of the Earth: initial KE = (1/2) m v_esc^2. The work done in lifting a body from the Earth's surface to an infinite distance equals the increase in potential energy: increase in PE = 0 - (-G M m / R) = G M m / R, where M and R are the mass and radius of the Earth. The body escapes from the gravitational field if its initial KE equals the increase in PE: (1/2) m v_esc^2 = G M m / R, or v_esc = sqrt(2GM/R) ... (4.14). As g = GM/R^2, or gR = GM/R, hence v_esc = sqrt(2gR) ... (4.15). The value of v_esc comes out to be approximately 11 km s^-1.
